chunks: Abu Basir narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a person performing tamattu‘ who intended to trim the hair but shaved his head. He said: “He must offer a blood-sacrifice that he spills, and when it is the Day of Sacrifice, he should pass the razor over his head when he intends to shave.”

key_terms.يَوْمُ النَّحْرِ: the Day of Sacrifice during hajj rites
key_terms.يُقَصِّرَ: to trim or shorten the hair as part of the rite

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a mutamatti‘ shaves his head instead of shortening his hair before completing the rites?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a mutamatti‘ who was supposed to shorten the hair but instead shaved the head. The Imam عليه السلام states that expiation is required, and on Yawm al-Nahr the person should still pass the razor over the head at the time of shaving.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2746 - Abu Basir narrated from Abu Abdullah (as):

I asked him about a person performing tamattu‘ who intended to trim their hair but instead shaved their head.
Imam (as) said: "They must offer a sheep as expiation. On the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Nahr), they should pass a razor over their head when they intend to shave."
